subject: Buying process & contract routing — owners, timing, and redline queue
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lisa@stromatech.com, tom.nguyen@stromatech.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-20T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Buying process & contract routing — owners, timing, and redline queue

Hi Lisa & Tom — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the buying path and who owns which queue.

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Technical fit: Stromatech wants predictable 99th pct latency for multi-tenant inference; will evaluate Dedicated vs Private.
- Decision criteria: latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, data residency, and audit log retention (2 years).
- Procurement: Procurement team and Legal/Privacy will run parallel reviews once we share NDA/MSA/DPA drafts.
- Economic buyer: you indicated finance lead (Lisa Morales) will sign off; technical champion is Tom.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send a single packet (NDA + MSA draft + one-page SOW) to procurement by EOD tomorrow.
2) Laura (CS lead) will prepare an integration checklist for Tom and his infra team.
3) Ben (pricing/econ) will follow up with a cost scenario for Dedicated capacity + burst profile.
4) Please confirm expected turnaround times for Legal redlines and whether you prefer sequential or parallel routing (example: Legal -> Procurement vs Legal+Procurement in parallel).

Attachments: I attached the MSA template and a simple NDA stub for you to circulate.

If this looks right, I'll queue the docs and open a shared Doc for redlines so we can triage reviewers.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood-MSA-template.docx (MSA template, redline-friendly), Stromatech-NDA-DRAFT.pdf (NDA stub)
From: lisa@stromatech.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.nguyen@stromatech.com, procurement@stromatech.com
Date: 2026-08-20T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buying process & contract routing — owners, timing, and redline queue

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Couple notes from Procurement/Legal side:

- Procurement (procurement@stromatech.com) will own commercial terms and PO cadence. Typical SLA: 7–10 business days to review commercial terms once Legal signs off.
- Legal (Tom) will run the MSA/DPA review. Our legal team prefers to receive MSA + DPA together; NDA can be handled separately if you need earlier access.
- Turn times: Legal aims for an initial redline within 5 business days for standard vendors, but for infra vendors with security implications (like Redwood) they may ask for 7–10 days and include a privacy engineer review.
- Routing preference: We usually do Legal + Procurement in parallel for larger deals, but Legal must sign off on privacy/security language before procurement completes the PO.

Action: I can be the economic approver for the initial PO but final sign-off will go to VP Finance (I will align with them). Please loop in our security contact (I'll introduce in a follow-up) so they can start the security questionnaire.

Approve you to send the packet to procurement now.

Lisa
Lisa Morales
Director, Data Platforms | Stromatech
lisa@stromatech.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: procurement@stromatech.com, tom.nguyen@stromatech.com, lisa@stromatech.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Packet: NDA + MSA draft + SOW (for routing)

Hi Procurement & Tom — per Lisa's OK, attaching the initial packet for your review. Short notes below:

- Attachment list: Stromatech-NDA-DRAFT.pdf, Redwood-MSA-template.docx, SOW-onepager.pdf
- Please use the shared Google Doc to redline the MSA so we can see comments in-line: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cMSA-redlines
- We can accept either redlines in Doc or a marked PDF. If you prefer DocuSign for signature-only flow after redlines, we can prepare that.
- Ben will follow up with a cost sensitivity sheet (Dedicated vs Private) targeted at your finance team by Friday.

A few clarifying questions that will help prioritize the routing:
1) Do you have a single reviewer for privacy/data residency matters or do you route privacy to a separate team?
2) Who should be the primary procurement contact for purchase order setup?

Thanks — we aim to turn initial comments around within 48 hours after we see your redlines.

Karthik
From: tom.nguyen@stromatech.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: lisa@stromatech.com, procurement@stromatech.com
Date: 2026-08-22T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packet: NDA + MSA draft + SOW (for routing)

On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 09:15 AM PDT karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Procurement & Tom — per Lisa's OK, attaching the initial packet for your review. Short notes below:
> 
> - Attachment list: Stromatech-NDA-DRAFT.pdf, Redwood-MSA-template.docx, SOW-onepager.pdf
> - Please use the shared Google Doc to redline the MSA so we can see comments in-line: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cMSA-redlines
> - We can accept either redlines in Doc or a marked PDF. If you prefer DocuSign for signature-only flow after redlines, we can prepare that.

Thanks Karthik — received. A couple quick items from Legal/security:

- Privacy reviewer: we have a privacy engineer (A. Patel) who will review data residency and logging requirements. I will loop her in shortly.
- DPA: please include a DPA appendix rather than inline clauses in the MSA; it helps our contract template consumption.
- Redline sequencing: we'll do a single pass of redlines and deliver comments in the Google Doc. Expect initial comments by Tue 2026-08-25.

One ask: could Redwood flag any non-starter clauses up front (e.g., indemnity cap, data residency hard requirements) so we can triage quickly? That will speed our review.

-Tom
Legal Counsel | Stromatech
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lisa@stromatech.com, tom.nguyen@stromatech.com, procurement@stromatech.com
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packet: NDA + MSA draft + SOW (for routing) — internal checklist + turnaround SLA

Hi all — Laura here from Customer Success. Quick internal note to set expectations on our side and make it easy for your reviewers: 

- I'll own the integration checklist and will publish it in the shared folder by tomorrow. That will include network rules, allowed IP ranges, KV cache behavior, and latency test plan.
- Ben: please confirm the cost scenarios you promised (Dedicated baseline, 95th pct throughput, burst pricing) so Lisa can attach to PO discussion.
- Karthik: we'll flag the following non-starter items up front in the Doc: indefinite retention of PII in logs (we store short-term only), and any obligations that require Redwood to disclose encryption keys.

SLA on our side: once we have Stromatech's initial redlines (expected Tue 8/25), CS + Legal + Pricing will aim to consolidate responses within 72 business hours. If there are high-impact privacy asks, we may need an extra 48 hours for engineering input.

We want to keep the sequencing: Legal & Privacy redline -> Redwood responses -> Procurement finalizes PO. Parallel routing is fine as long as Legal signs off on privacy clauses before PO is issued.

Thanks — I'll post the checklist and a one-page integration summary shortly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
